The Sub-Inspector of Police, Subramanyapura Police Station, Bengaluru City has filed Police Report against the above named accused alleging that she has committed the offences punishable under Sections 323, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. The Prosecution case in brief is that the accused is the wife of CW1 Dr.Sanjeev Hiremath.
There are matrimonial differences between them.
Since, their matrimonial differences were not solved inspite of many panchayaths were convened, the accused is residing separately in another house belongs to CW1 along with her children.
On 05.05.2017, CW1 went to Kerala State on his work.

On that day, the accused came to the house of CW1 bearing No.02, 19th Cross, 13th Main Road, Krishod Garden, Revenue Layout, Subramanyapura, Bengaluru - 560 061 within the territorial jurisdiction of Subramanyapura Police Station, Bengaluru City; picked up quarrel with CW2 and CW3 who were in the said house; abused them in filthy languages; gave life threat stating that if they are not vacated the house, she will show an end to them and voluntarily caused simple hurt to them by beating them with her hands.
Thereby, the accused has committed the offences punishable under Sections 323, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code.
3. Based on the First Information of CW1, the crime was registered in Crime No.244/2017 at Subramanyapura Police Station, Bengaluru City.
During Investigation, the accused has appeared before this Court and enlarged on bail.

On completion of the investigation, the Sub-Inspector of Police, Subramanyapura Police Station, Bengaluru City filed Police Report against the accused alleging that she has committed the offences punishable under Sections 323, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code.
After taking cognizance of the said offences, the process was issued to the accused.
She has appeared before this Court.
The copies of the Police Report and other prosecution papers are furnished to the accused under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.

After hearing, since there were grounds for presuming that the accused has committed offences triable by this Court, charges for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code have been framed and read over to her in Kannada language.
She has pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.

4. To prove the charges framed against the accused, out of 6 witnesses cited by the Investigation Officer in the Police Report, the Prosecution has produced the oral evidences of only four witnesses as PW1 to PW4.

Among them, PW1 Dr.Sanjeev Hiremath is the First Informant and the Mahazar witness, PW2 is Andanaiah and PW3 Shakunthala Hiremath are the injured witnesses and PW4 Dr.Sanjeev Hiremat vs Dr.Namratha on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161186737/
2 Vajramuni K. is the Investigation Officer of this case.
The Prosecution has also produced the documentary evidences in Ex.P1 to Ex.P4.
Among them, Ex.P1 is the First Information, Ex.P2 is the Spot Mahazar, Ex.P3 is the First Information Report and Ex.P4 is the Notice.
During Cross-examination of PW2, Ex.D1 and Ex.D2 were marked on behalf of the accused on confrontation.
Among them, Ex.D1 is the Book written by PW2 and Ex.D2 is the certified copy of the Vakalath.
During Cross-examination of PW1, Ex.D3 to Ex.D8 were marked on behalf of the accused on confrontation.

Among them, Ex.D3 is the Pendrive, Ex.D4 is the the certified copy of the Petition in Criminal Misc.No.3914/2017, Ex.D5 is the Copy of Discharge Summary and Ex.D6 to Ex.D8 are the Photographs of the accused.

5. After completion of the prosecution evidences, for the purpose of enabling the accused personally to explain any circumstances appearing in the evidences of the prosecution against her, examined the accused under Section 313 of Cr.P.C.
The accused during her examination under Section 313 of Cr.P.C., has denied the entire Prosecution evidences which are incriminating against her with regard to the alleged incident dated 05.05.2017.
She has submitted that she has no defence evidence.
She filed her Written Statement making counter allegations against PW2 and PW3 that they gave life threat to her and she has stated that she is innocent of the alleged offences.
6. Heard the arguments of the learned Senior Assistant Public Prosecutor and the learned Counsel for the accused.

The learned Senior Assistant Public Prosecutor has argued that from the evidences of PW1 to PW3 and the contents of Ex.P1, the prosecution has proved the guilt of the accused for the offences charged against her.
The Investigation Officer has given his evidences with regard to the Investigation conducted by him.
Nothing has been elicited in his cross- examination to disbelieve his evidences deposed in his examination-in-chief.
Hence, prayed to convict the accused for the charges framed against her.
7. Per contra, the arguments of the learned Counsel for the accused are that there is a delay of seven to eight days in lodging the First Information.
The delay in lodging the First Information is not explained by the prosecution.
In fact, it is admitted fact that on the date of alleged incident itself, the Police came to the house.
If really such incident took place, there were every possibility of immediate lodging the First Information.
This is a counter blast to the case registered by the accused on 06.05.2017 against PW1 to PW3 at Banashankari Police Station in Crime No.145/2017.
The accused has produced the documentary evidences to prove that on 06.05.2017, Crime No.145/2017 was registered by the accused against PW1 to PW3 at Banashankari Police Station.
After the alleged incident, PW2 wrote in Ex.D1 that the accused is good daughter-in-law for him.
Hence, prayed to acquit the accused.
8. Perused the materials available on record.

9. The points for determination are;
1.
Whether prosecution has proved the offences charged against the accused persons for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code beyond reasonable doubt?

Dr.Sanjeev Hiremat vs Dr.Namratha on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161186737/
3 2.
What order or sentence?

10. My answers to the above points are as follows:
 Point No.1 : In the Negative,
 Point No.2 : As per final order for the following;
 REASONS 11. POINT No.1 :- As per the case of the prosecution, based on Ex.P1 given by PW1, the crime has been registered in Crime No.244/2017 and on investigation, since, there are evidences collected by the Investigation Officer to prosecute the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 323,
504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, the Police Report was filed.

In the First Information - Ex.P1,
there are statements of PW1 with regard to the alleged incident committed by the accused.

12. PW1 in his examination-in-chief has deposed that on 05.05.2017 at 12.30 p.m., the accused came to his house; abused his parents in filthy languages; gave life threat to them; she beaten on the cheek of PW2 with her hands; when his mother pacified, she was also pushed by the accused; she gave life threat stating that if they have not vacated the house, she will not leave them; on 06.05.2017, she came again and did the very same acts did on the previous day and threatened his parents.
13. It appears from the contents of Ex.P1 and the oral evidences of PW1 that he is not an eyewitness of the incident.
PW2 and PW3 are the parents of PW1 on whom, the accused did the alleged overt acts.

PW1 has deposed in his examination-in-chief that on 05.05.2017, when he, PW1 and CW4 were at house, at about 12.00 p.m., the accused came; abused him in filthy languages by using the words "

   
 

 
   

, 
    

  
, 
     
 

 
 
   
 
  

   
    "; thrown their cloths, suitcases and bags out of the house; she took the files and valuable things belongs to PW1 from the wardrobe of his room; when he told her that let she take them after his son came, she beaten on his cheek; at that time, he lost his balance; while PW3 hold him, the accused beaten her and pushed her; she threatened that if they are not gone out of the house, she will called Police and send them out; on 06.05.2017, again the accused came and threatened them that she will see them and their son by coming out and they will show an end to them.

Dr.Sanjeev Hiremat vs Dr.Namratha on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161186737/
4 14.

PW3 has deposed in her examination-in-chief that on 05.05.2017, when she, her husband and CW4 were at house, the accused came at about 12.00 p.m.; she told why they came and whether it is their house; at that time, she told that as her son told them to come, they came; at that time, the accused with angry thrown their cloths, suitcases and bags out of the house; she took the files and valuable things belongs to PW1 from the wardrobe of his room; when PW2 told her that let she take them after his son came, she beaten on his cheek; at that time, he lost his balance; while she hold him, the accused beaten her; she threatened that if they are not gone out of the house, she will called Police and send them out; on 06.05.2017, again the accused came; abused them in filthy languages and threatened them that she will see them and their son by coming out and they will show an end to them.
15. PW4 is the Investigation Officer of this case.

He has deposed in his examination-in-chief that on 13.05.2017 at 3.40 p.m., when he was In-Charge of the Police Station, he received the First Information given by PW1 as per Ex.P1; registered the crime; forwarded the First Information Report to the Court as per Ex.P3; on the same day he conducted the Mahazar in the place of incident between 4.15 p.m. to 5.15 p.m. as per Ex.P2 in the presence of CW4 and CW5; recorded the Witness Statements of PW2, PW3 and CW4; on 09.10.2017, he gave Notice to the accused as per Ex.P4; on 03.11.2017, he enquired the accused and filed the Police Report after completion of investigation.
16. PW1 has deposed in his examination-in-chief that after he gave First Information, the Police came to his house and conducted Mahazar as per Ex.
Admittedly, PW1 is not an eyewitness of the incident.
His statements in Ex.P1 and oral evidences deposed by him before the Court are only hearsay evidences.
As per the allegations made in Ex.P1 and the oral evidences of PW1 to PW3, the alleged incidents were taken place on 05.05.2017 and 06.05.2017.
As per the contents of Ex.P1 and the oral evidences of PW1, on 07.05.2017, PW1 came to his house from Thiruvananthapuram.
As per the contents of Ex.P1 and the oral evidences of PW1 to PW3, on 11.05.2017, PW2 and PW3 told about the alleged incident to PW1.
Admittedly, on 13.05.2017, the First Information was given by PW1 to PW4.
It is stated in Ex.P1 and PW1 has deposed in his examination-in-chief that after he came on 07.05.2017, he was busy for two days.
Even if, PW1 came to know about the alleged incident only on 11.05.2017, there is no reason assigned for delay of two days caused in lodging the First Information.
The reason is also not assigned why PW2 and PW3 have not lodged the First Information about the alleged incident till PW1 lodged the First Information as per Ex.P1.
Admittedly, on 05.05.2017 itself, the Police came to the house of PW1 and at that time, PW2 and PW3 were very much present.
It is not their evidences that at that time, they tried to give First Information about the alleged incident.

Admittedly, on 06.05.2017, Crime No.145/2017 was registered at Banashankari Police Station against PW1 to PW3 based on the First Information given by the accused herein for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 and 506 R/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
In Ex.D4, this fact is pleaded on behalf of PW1 to PW3.

PW1 in his cross-examination has admitted that he was aware the fact that the Police of Banashankari Police Station were visited to his house two days prior to giving the First Information of this crime.
But, he has expressed his ignorance that such visit was made with regard to Crime No.145/2017.
PW2 has admitted in his cross-examination that on 07.05.2017, the Police conducted Mahazar at the house of PW1.

PW3 has denied in her cross-examination that on Dr.Sanjeev Hiremat vs Dr.Namratha on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161186737/
5 07.05.2017, the Police of Banashankari Police Station have conducted Mahazar at the house of PW1.
But, she has deposed in her cross-examination that as per her version, the Police came on 12th or 13th May 2015.
It shows that after registering the crime by the accused in Crime No.145/2017 and the Mahazar conducted at the house of PW1, this crime was registered by PW1.

Therefore, the delay of seven days in lodging the First Information play a vital role to raise a suspicion with regard to the allegations made in Ex.P1.
18.
During investigation, PW4 has recorded the Witness Statements of PW2 and PW3.
Their statements given before the Investigation Officer are so accurate and verbatim between each other.
But, in Ex.P1, it is not stated that the accused has beaten PW3 also.

As per the Witness Statements given before the Investigation Officer by PW2 and PW3, the accused pushed PW2; he fell down; he got up with the help of his wife i.e., PW3 and at that time, the accused beaten on his cheek with her hands and when PW3 came across, the accused has beaten on her with hands.
This incident is dated 05.05.2017.

But, PW2 has deposed in his examination-in- chief that 05.05.2017, the accused beaten on his cheek with her hands; when he lost consciousness, his wife i.e., PW3 hold him and at that time, the accused beaten PW3 and pushed her.
PW1 has deposed in his examination-in-chief that the accused beaten on the cheek of PW2 with her hands and when PW3 went to pacify it, the accused pushed her.
PW2 has admitted in his cross-examination that when his examination-in-chief was conducted, he discussed about the case with his son and deposed his evidence before the Court.
PW3 has deposed in her examination-in-chief that the accused beaten on the cheek of PW2; at that time, PW2 lost his balance and when she went to hold him, the accused beaten her with hands.

These are three difference versions of PW1 to PW3 appearing in their oral evidences deposed in their examination-in-chief and they are contrary to the statements given by PW2 and PW3 before the Investigation Officer and also the contents of Ex.P1.
Like wise, the words used by the accused to abuse PW2 and PW3 and to give life threat to them are also contrary between each other.
This is yet another suspicious circumstance appearing in the evidences of the Prosecution.

The delay in lodging the First Information and the above contradictions appearing in the oral evidences of PW1 to PW3 are considered along with the contents of Ex.P1, it is a clear case that the present First Information has been lodged as a counterblast to the crime registered by the accused herein against PW1 to PW3 in Crime No.145/2017 on the file of Banashankari Police Station.

Under these circumstances, I am holding that the Prosecution has not proved the guilt of the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code beyond all reasonable doubt.
19. In the written statement filed by the accused, she has denied the commission of the alleged offences by her on PW1 to PW3.
It appears from the admitted videos in Ex.P3 that on some other day, the incident was taken place and in the said incident, the accused has not committed any such overt act as alleged herein.
Hence, I answer Point No.1 in the Negative.

20. POINT No.2 :- For the reasons stated in Point No.1, the Prosecution has not proved the guilt of the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code beyond all reasonable doubt.
Therefore, the accused is not found guilty for the aforesaid offences charged against her.
